title: bug: local-runner vm-control canonicalProjectPath matches /mnt/<d> on the raw string, so a relative or non-normalized WSL project path gets a different VM ledger dir and readDaemonInfo refuses its live daemon
description:
Found by architect-4ae016fb while planning task-ea57601d (the moe-proxy comparableProjectPath fix). scripts/local-runner/vm-control.mjs canonicalProjectPath (about line 31) is a port of moe-proxy's comparableProjectPath, added by CQ-I03a (task-c0b0775f), and it has the same flaw. It detects the drive-letter and /mnt/<d> forms on the raw trimmed string only.

On WSL that gives two wrong results:
- A relative path, e.g. "." run from /mnt/d/projexts/moes, misses both raw regexes. It goes through path.resolve, and the result "/mnt/d/projexts/moes" is returned unconverted instead of "d:/projexts/moes".
- A non-normalized /mnt path keeps its raw rest, e.g. "/mnt/d/projexts/../projexts/moes" or "/mnt/d//projexts/moes".

Effects:
- ownedLedgerDir (about line 44) hashes the canonical string, so the same project gets a different ~/.moe/runner-state/<hash>/vms ledger dir.
- readDaemonInfo (line 126) compares canonicalProjectPath(info.projectPath) with canonicalProjectPath(projectPath), so it throws unreachable for the project's own live daemon.

Fix shape: mirror whatever rule task-ea57601d lands: resolve or normalize before detecting the special forms, and POSIX-normalize the /mnt rest. That way the proxy and its port agree; ideally a shared test table pins both.

Compatibility, the reason this is its own row: changing the canonical form changes ownedLedgerDir's hash for the inputs that were mis-keyed. An input that is already canonical (an absolute, normalized D:/x, D:\x, /mnt/d/x or POSIX path) must hash to the byte-identical ledger dir it does today, so no existing VM ledger is orphaned.
definitionOfDone: canonicalProjectPath maps a relative path that resolves under /mnt/<d>/..., and a non-normalized /mnt/<d> path (".." or "." segments, doubled or trailing slashes), to the same key as the normalized absolute form. Each case is a test in scripts/tests/local-runner-vm-control.test.mjs.

For already-canonical inputs (D:/x, D:\x, /mnt/d/x and a POSIX absolute path), canonicalProjectPath and ownedLedgerDir return results byte-identical to the pre-fix code, pinned as literal expected values in a test.
readDaemonInfo accepts a daemon.json whose projectPath differs from the caller's only by those forms, and still throws unreachable for a different project. Both cases are tested.
